Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes which has a section. Then the
functor
<MATHSEG_0001>descent data for <MATHSEG_0002>tale sheaves wrt <MATHSEG_0003>
sending <MATH_0002> in <MATH_0003> to the canonical descent datum
is an equivalence of categories.

Let <MATH_0001> be a surjective integral morphism of schemes.
The functor
<MATHSEG_0001>descent data for <MATHSEG_0002>tale sheaves wrt <MATHSEG_0003>
is an equivalence of categories.

Let <MATH_0001> be a surjective proper morphism of schemes.
The functor
<MATHSEG_0001>descent data for <MATHSEG_0002>tale sheaves wrt <MATHSEG_0003>
is an equivalence of categories.

source_text:
Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes. Let <MATH_0002> be a surjective
integral morphism of schemes or a surjective proper morphism of schemes.
If the functors
<MATHSEG_0001>descent data for <MATHSEG_0002>tale sheaves wrt <MATHSEG_0003>
and
<MATHSEG_0004>descent data for <MATHSEG_0005>tale sheaves wrt <MATHSEG_0006>
are equivalences of categories, then
<MATHSEG_0007>descent data for <MATHSEG_0008>tale sheaves wrt <MATHSEG_0009>
is an equivalence.

Let <MATH_0001> be a morphism of schemes which is
surjective, flat, locally of finite presentation.
The functor
<MATHSEG_0001>descent data for <MATHSEG_0002>tale sheaves wrt <MATHSEG_0003>
is an equivalence of categories.

\longrightarrow

$$
